# aterm-gui: spec recovery from its unit tests

> Status 2026-10-16, after the merge with the tests-and-gates audit: the rows naming 749 tests it
> deleted and 112 specs whose functions it deleted are gone, and the spec rows no longer cite
> those tests. Counts elsewhere in this file were taken before. The Windows app platform came
> back afterwards, and with it its 43 spec rows, five §2 rows, two §3 entries and the citations
> of its restored tests.

> Status 2026-10-17: 5 more spec rows whose functions the audit deleted are gone, and so are 43 §2
> rows whose tests are gone. Tests and functions already gone before the merge (Smart Titles, the
> Settings pager and its picker paging, Trail Packs) are out of §1 too: 7 more spec rows are gone,
> and the other rows no longer cite those tests or name those functions and features.

> Status 2026-10-20, predictive editing increment 2's GUI wiring: `predict-edit-keys` and
> `render-paint-prediction-chain` are new rows, written with the code they state and the tests named
> in them run; `classify-press-keypad-fold` gains the keypad arrow's exception, `predict-privacy` says
> a bare arrow is modelled now, and `render-paint-prediction-ghosts` states the painter's refusal, its
> `Option` answer and the closure's `overlay_frame`, which the rows said otherwise before.
>
> 2026-10-20, after review of that wiring: the keypad arrow's exception was stated from a false encoder
> fact (DECKPAM does not change a keypad arrow's bytes; the legacy encoder sends `NumpadArrowLeft` as
> `ArrowLeft`), so a keypad arrow is an edit key now and only a Kitty mode that reports the keypad routes
> it as unmodelled input, as it does a locked arrow (`classify-press-keypad-fold`, `predict-edit-keys`);
> the no-echo gate `predict-edit-keys` named for edit keys did not exist (the tty verdict was read for
> typed text alone) and now does; and `render-paint-prediction-chain` names a test of the single-pane
> path, which had none.

> Status 2026-10-20, the disk walker (system awareness P2d): `materialize-policy` left with its
> code, which moved to `aterm-diskwalk`'s `iopol` (the design's crate table); its two tests run there.

> Status 2026-10-20, lineage reaches the fabric endpoint (bridge lane 3): `fab-log-lineage` is a new
> row, written with the code it states and the tests named in it run; `fab-log-switch` now says it is
> the contract of the bare `link log <ident>`, which a moved generation is told only when its bridge
> cannot say where it continues (a bridge before lane 3, or no lineage to go by). After review the
> row says the endpoint applies each move once with no window of its own (the eight-move window of
> the first cut is gone), and names the tests that hold a verdict, an `await inbox re=` and the
> refill floor across a move, and a nine-move chain.

> Status 2026-10-21, the events pace out of the fabric's path: `subscribe-push-semantics` now says a
> record (a timeline row, a booked resize row, a landed turn) is read at once whatever the events
> pace's window, which holds only the PTY reader's rings, and bounds an output flood's reads at
> ceil(T/EVENTS_PACE)+1 plus one per record; `session-watchers-coalescing-wake` states the record
> count the producers step. Both are written with the code they state, and the tests they gain ran.

> Status 2026-10-16: this is the crate's migration worklist. Nothing has been proved yet. The tests were
> read in 26 chunks. This file is assembled mechanically from the chunk results, because one merge
> could not hold them all. Specs are **not yet deduplicated across chunks**: ids that collided got a `-N`
> suffix, and two chunks may state the same property. The tests in §2 that were confirmed to sample no
> spec are being deleted separately. Rows whose code the sessions-as-subagents removals deleted (the
> embedded operator, the network drive's listener, its saved connections and `dial`; design §7) are
> dropped, and rows that only named an operator facet of code that stays are restated without it.
> Smart Titles, retired on main by `64b1d6833`, is dropped the same way: its own rows go, and mixed
> rows lose its facets and test names. So are the connection card and the drag-to-connect gesture,
> deleted with the owner surfaces (`docs/DESIGN-owner-surfaces-2026-10-16.md` S12): the tab's
> status-mark cell they used is the `Marks` hit now, whose press opens the tab menu.

Source: `crates/aterm-gui` (read only). Nothing was compiled or run; every claim comes from reading the code.

Result: **2589 specs** from **7940 tests read**, naming about 7981 subsumed tests. **179 tests** were proposed as samples of no spec (§2). 325 tests looked suspicious (§3).

After the reading, the strain row's removal (2026-10-16, CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]`) took its seven host specs (`own-jobs-registry`, `own-jobs-with-rows`, `remote-program-set`, `strain-sample-admission`, `strain-deadline-gate`, `strain-row-lifecycle`, `freeze-near-key-match`) and their tests out of the 2597 the reading found, and `abs-rows-dense-read` left with the GUI's own absolute-row readers for aterm-core's one search-row reader (aterm-core's spec of that name); the test counts are the reading's.

The merge of the session log's phase 3A (2026-10-17) reworded the rows its code contradicts (`CDN-first-line-scope`, `leading-options-grammar`, `auth-handshake-deadline`, `edge-grant-lifecycle`, `connection-verbs`, `required-op-table`, `subscribe-push-semantics`, `sub-requested-grammar`, `sub-membership-announcement-order`): the harness token, `cause=`, the reserved actor words, `mark` and the `log` stream. Those rows also cite phase 3A's tests of what they now state; the counts above do not include them.

That is one window `WindowId(0)` at 24x80, session 0 registered and pooled, no OS window, `headless = true`. `Reach`: the Apps reachable from `App0` by the App's own operations (`push_stub_tab`, `split_active_*`, `open_settings_tab`, `insert_logical_window`, `close_*`, `restore_into_window`, `adopt_orphan_shells_as_tabs`, `exit_session_logical`, find/rename/menu entry points). Specs are stated for every such input. - `Inv(app)`: `structural_invariants_ok()`, the conjunction checked by `structural_invariant_violation()`. - `Tabs(app,w)`: the canonical `tab_set` of window w. Each tab is a `SplitTree<ViewId>` with focus and zoom; `view_store` resolves each view to `Terminal(session)` or `Native(instance)`. `Proj(app,w)`: the legacy terminal-only projection `layouts`/`tabs: TabIndex`. - `Cap(app)`: `capture_restore_manifest()`. `HCap(app)`: `capture_handoff_layout()`. `Wire(m) = m.to_toml()`, `Parse(s) = RestoreManifest::from_toml(s)`. `Topo(m) = commit_layout_topology(m)`. `Carry(m) = commit_agent_carry(m)`. - `Meta(s)`: the `SessionMeta` read through the registry handle of pool session s (`registry_meta`). The user fields are user_title, description, icon, role, attention, questions. `Sanitize_f`: the session_timeline sanitizer for field f. It strips control, bidi, zero-width and line/paragraph separators, trims, bounds to the `META_*_MAX` limits, keeps ZWJ clusters, and keeps questions only within `QUESTIONS_POLICY_WORDS`. - `Handed`: the `seamless_adopt` list of `spawn::Adopted` shells, keyed by `local_id`. `Shown(app)`: for each window, tab and leaf, the `handoff_local_id` of the pane's session (`shown_shells`). `Named(L)`: the same shape read off a layout's terminal leaves. - `Ledger`: the session_store roster journal of `Exited` rows `(reason, actor)`. - `Policy`: `close_confirm ∈ {Interactive, Programmatic, WireRefuseBusy}`. - `Facts(s)`: `SearchState::count_facts()`. `Abs(s,i) = (match_base_y + matches[i].row, matches[i].col)`. - `M ⊑ Model`: Tier-1 refinement. Each real step, projected to the model's variables, is admitted by exactly the named action (`interp::admits` / `assert_transition`), every invariant holds, and each `Buggy=1` mutant is refused at its own action. - `FP`: any repaint/glance/strip fingerprint (FNV-1a). The claimable spec is that FP is a deterministic function of exactly the rendered fields it documents. Injectivity is NOT claimable (hash collisions).

Shorthand: auto(m) = m.is_automatic() for ApplyMode ∈ {Automatic, AutomaticPastGrace, Immediate}. App = the GUI App state (App::headless_for_test() in tests); "&mut self App" means the spec is a contract on an App method and needs certified &self/&mut self views (gap 2). Model(M) = the ty_model! machine aterm_spec::derive::M; "conforms/refines" = every concrete step, projected onto M's variables, is the named M action with every invariant kept, and the Buggy=1 mutant (negative control) is rejected. That is the derive.rs rule, so negative-control tests are folded into their conformance spec. activity(m) = poll(2) on master fd m reports POLLIN and no HUP/ERR/NVAL. closed(m) = poll reports HUP|ERR|NVAL. View/Obs of parser state reuse crates/aterm-parser/SPECS.md (cross-crate, gap 12). Durations are written in ms or s. Gap numbers refer to AUDIT section 7: 1 non-scalar carriers, 2 &self/&mut self views, 3 E6 body widening, 4 callee-ensures composition, 5 quantified clauses, 7 loops, 8 effects, 9 proc-macro boundary, 10 model-to-code refinement, 12 cross-crate citation, 13 threads/closures.
- chunk 8: Paths are crate-relative to crates/aterm-gui. Pty(s) = the byte sequence written to session s's PTY sink (SinkWriter) during a step; "types nothing" means Pty(s) = []. Glass = the frame's RenderCell rows after App::splice_claude_footer; Hits(w) = WindowLights.hits (one LightHit per painted chip cell, chip=None for the blank between two chips). Rung order LADDER = [Revealed, Drawn, NoLight, AutopilotOnly, GlyphOnly]. drawn_at(s,now,sel,hov,keep)(c) := keep.keeps(c) && (c = Autopilot => s.autopilot is Some(v) with v != Unhosted) && (c = Light(l) => deviates(l,s.shown) || pending=l || live refusal=l || live notice=l || sel.or(hov)=c || (keep=Revealed && sel!=None && s.shown.state(l)!=Unknown)); "live" means until > now. H(...) = std DefaultHasher over the listed fields; no spec claims H is injective, only that a result is a function of exactly the listed fields (and |1 makes it nonzero). FS = abstract file system: path -> entry {kind: file|dir|symlink(target)|fifo|socket, bytes, mode, uid, dev, ino, nlink, ctime}; "never through a link" = no write/remove reaches an entry other than the named one. "serving lane" = a thread inside ServingFd::enter(stream); a caller is HUNG UP iff every descriptor of the peer end is closed (a write-side shutdown is not). Model refinement R(model, proj) = every observed step of the shipping code, projected by proj, is a transition the derived aterm_spec model admits under the named action, and the model's invariants hold after it. Time values are Instant/Duration treated as non-negative integers with saturating subtraction. Gap numbers are AUDIT section 7 rows.
- chunk 9: Shared notation (aterm-gui chunk 9, crates/aterm-gui/src/control_*). - Toks(s) = s.split_whitespace(); Trim(s) = s.trim(). 'Grammar G parses s to v' means: parse(s)=Ok(v) iff s is in L(G) with denotation v, and parse(s)=Err(U) with U the verb's one usage line otherwise. Every parser spec below has that shape: the set of accepted strings and the value, not sample strings. - Reach(T) = Terminals reachable from Terminal::new(r,c) (r,c>=1) by any finite sequence of process/process_at, resize, scroll_display, apply_config, text_selection_mut ops, reset, clear_scrollback, set_cell_pixel_size, set_scrollback_line_limit, advance_kitty_animations, alt-archive setters, and Arc replacement of the Terminal behind an Arc<Mutex<_>>. - Frame(t) = serialize_styled_frame(&gather_styled_frame(t)), the full `screen` reply without its trailing etag key. - Rows(t) = screen_text(t).split_terminator('\n'): the untrimmed visible rows `text` sends, one per grid row. - LogicalLines(t) = the maximal soft-wrap runs of the active grid's retained history plus screen. Each run is joined row by row, every row padded to its full cell width as drawn (blank rows included), and keyed by the absolute row of the run's head. Cell widths are the stored cells, not a re-measure. - RefSearch(t,q) = all matches of q (literal or regex, case flag) over LogicalLines(t). Each is re-expressed as (abs_row, col, len_cells) at the physical row/cell where the match's first grapheme is drawn, with ^/$ binding to logical-line ends. - Model(m) = an aterm_spec ty_model! / aterm_spec::derive model. 'Refines Model(m) under pi' means every shipping step projects through pi to an enabled model action with the same successor, and pi(init)=Init. - App = crate::App built by App::headless_for_test (headless flag as stated). Scope = Owner | Bridge | Edge(token). - WireTwin(text,json): the set of key=value keys of the text form equals the key set of the JSON object and the values agree (text '-'/'none' <-> JSON null; self-labelling 'a:1,b:2' <-> object). - Gap numbers refer to docs/AUDIT-trust-for-test-migration-2026-10-15.md section 7; 0 = only the seal upgrade.

- chunk 11: Test ids are "crates/aterm-gui/src/<file>.rs::<fn>". I read all 368 #[test] fns in the 22 files of chunk aterm-gui/11. The chunk file says 343; the per-file grep and the extraction both find 368 (debugger_access 25, defterm_win 10, desk 3, desktop_alert_debt_conformance 1, devtools_helper 23, devtools_watch 2, diagnostics 67, document_journal_conformance 1, document_store 12, document_store_conformance 2, driver_geometry_conformance 10, dsu_quiescence_conformance 2, echo_rtt 9, editor_carry_conformance 16, exceptions_host 14, explorer_win 1, fabric 105, fabric_launch 13, file_picker_win 10, find_bar 20, fleet_watch 3, since renamed sibling_scan, which holds 2, foreground_handback 19). Nothing was compiled or run. Notation: - "refines model M under projection pi" (kind=refinement): each step of the composed production code, mapped through the projection fn of that conformance module (debugger_access::conformance, close_projection, publication_projection, the journal projection, the Rig::project fns of driver_geometry / dsu_quiescence / editor_carry / desktop_alert_debt, spawn::foreground_handback_conformance::project_ownership), is a step that the ty_model! model M in aterm_spec::derive admits. Each model guard equals what the code did, and every M invariant holds afterwards. The conformance test's negative controls (Buggy=k successors, fault-injected compositions, hand-built bad states) become the proof's required mutation or negative control (PLAN "done" item 3). A "mark" is '…'. ord(i) is the 1-based tab position i+1 written in decimal. - Segs(cols,n,md,active,upd[,slot]) is the output of layout_segments_with_metadata / layout_segments_with_version. layout_segments(cols,n,a,u) = Segs with PLAIN_TAB metadata. Chips(S) are the segments of kind Select(i). seated(S) = {i | Select(i) ∈ S}. A chip's title window is avail(seg) = title_end - title_start from tab_content_layout(seg, md[i]). - Labels(S,titles,md,active) = distinct_chip_labels(...), indexed by tab. active* = min(active, n-1), the clamp layout_segments applies. - Wire(frames, ts) is the bytes Egress writes for one producer in one wake: begin_wake, then send(frames). text(frames) is the concatenation of the frames' segments. - A Watch's watermarks are (last_sent_seq, last_alt, last_cursor, last_text, last_rows_hash, last_cells_etag, last_block_id, last_timeline_id, last_resize_id, last_turn_id, last_title, last_bell, last_mail_id). - Rec is a TemporalRecorder. live(Rec) is its EventLog live ring in seq order. Blobs is the FIFO window [next_blob - |blobs|, next_blob). - PlanOK(plan,bounds): every leaf rect has width ≥ 0 and height ≥ 0 and lies inside bounds (to f32::EPSILON). Leaf order equals tree.leaves(). Dividers and leaves are pairwise disjoint. - A refinement spec means: for every real operation, project(before) → project(after) is a transition the named ty_model! model admits, and the named invariant holds. A negative control (a mutated projection) must be rejected. This is the conformance-test shape AGENTS.md requires (aterm-spec derive). - Gap numbers refer to AUDIT section 7. Most specs here need gap 1 (String/Vec/struct carriers), 3 (body widening), 5 (quantifiers) and 7 (loops). Gaps 8, 10 and 13 apply where fs, models or threads are involved.
- chunk 25: Paths are relative to crates/aterm-gui/src. Message shape: for an aterm_messages::Message m, m.hold in {Live{stale_after}, LogOnly (a RECORD: logged, never on glass), Default, For(d), STANDING}; m.tag, m.severity, m.title, m.detail: Vec<String>, m.key, m.actions: Vec<Intent>, m.glyph, m.meter{fill_permille, stats, busy, amount, load}, m.excerpt, m.finished. ShapeOK(m) := chars(m.title) <= TITLE_CAP && m.glyph in Glyph::ALLOWED \ {Glyph::FALLBACK} && message_reporters::attention(m) is Ok. Words(xs) := the whitespace-split words of xs joined in order. sanitize := atpkg::progress::sanitize_for_tty (control chars removed). App-level observations (headless App::headless_for_test): Band(app) = app.messages.live_rows(); Log(app) = app.messages.log().records(); Rev(app) = app.messages.revision(); Digest(app) = app.messages.digest().entries. Look(rows) := app.apply_agent_upgrades(rows). For aterm_agent::harness::upgrade_drive::Row r: Attn(r,now) = r.attention(now) in {Quiet, Fault(k), Digest(k), Interrupt(k)}. Watchdog: Park(bc) := bc in {Startup, AboutToWait, UpdateHandoff, Modal}; SpinStall(bc) := bc not in {Startup, UpdateHandoff, Modal}. Sampler runs on a synthetic clock (Instant values passed in). Trail audio: Host = TrailAudio, Cap = COMMAND_CAPACITY, Budget = REOPEN_BUDGET. 'Refines M' means: every real step, projected by the file's own projection fn, is in M.successors(action, projected_before), every model invariant holds on every projected state, and the Buggy=1 variant rejects the replayed defect (the negative control the plan requires). Spec ids are crate-local (prefix gui25-).

Notation. - WS = restore::WindowShow {fullscreen, minimized: Option<bool>, z_order: Option<u32>, key: Option<bool>}; UNKNOWN = all None; is_unknown(s) <=> s == UNKNOWN. - For a manifest ws: &[(W, WS)] with distinct W: F(ws) = stable sort of ws by z_order.unwrap_or(u32::MAX), giving front-to-back order with ties in manifest order. M0 = [w in F | show.minimized == Some(true)]. M = M0, except on lane Cold when |M0| = |F|, where M = M0 \ {F[0].w}. V = [w in F | w not in M]. - key(ws,lane) = the first w in MANIFEST order with show.key == Some(true) and w in V, else V.first(). - btf_k(L) = reverse(L), then the key (if present in it) moved to the end. - EmptyPlan = ShowPlan{minimize:[], raise:[], key:None, fullscreen:[], focus_seed:[]}. - Carry(app) = app.carried_window_show; Live(app) = keys of app.windows. - Seam = one of settle_carried_window_show, settle_carried_window_show_at_proof, commit_carried_window_show(typed), carried_window_show_focus_event(w). Each is applied after on_focus, in the order the Focused arm uses. - may_stack(seam) = true for _at_proof, else app.handoff_ready.is_none(). - InFront(app,c) = exists w in c.plan.focus_seed with w in c.heard and app.windows[w].focused. - Typed(app) = pre_commit_typed_windows(app) = [winit_to_window[id] | (id, ev) in handoff_deferred_input, ev is KeyboardInput or Ime, id mapped], in queue order. - WorkCounters: the cfg(test) thread-local ghost counters in src/work_counts.rs (plans_built at App::plan_tab, latency_stamps_touched, status_probes, title_tab_touches, retained_records_touched). Specs W1-W5 treat them as ghost cost counters on the production function. The audit table has no gap row for ghost cost instrumentation. It is closest to 2 plus 7. - Model = aterm_models_update::native_update_window_show_model (NativeUpdateWindowShow, ty_model!). Proj = window_show_conformance::Rig::project.

lane-tenure-refinement	refinement	control_lanes::Lanes::{new,start,publish,admit}, control_lanes::Census, control_lanes parker loop, control::note_connection_claim, control::serving_connection	The shipping Lanes refine control_lane_tenure_model under pi = (Census, requests in flight per lane kind, arrivals, busied) at every quiescent point. An authenticated idle connection is parked, never held on a request lane (NoIdleHold). So while placed open < limits.open a fresh client is admitted and served at once, whatever idle or waiting drivers exist (NoRefusalByIdleDriver). At placed open = limits.open a fresh client is handed to the parker (Hand), as many at once as are parked, each owed one; the parker parks it in the slots of a connection that ended since, or else of the stalest parked connection that gives way (made its handshake, holds no live connection-bound claim; then the one whose peer moved no byte longest), which is closed while open stays at the cap (Place); a live claim holder and a connection still making its handshake are spared (Spare, Unspare); release or expiry makes a former claimant eligible again without losing its final Drop cleanup, and with none to give way the fresh client is answered busy (TurnAway). So it is refused only when every request lane works or no parked connection gives way that an earlier fresh client is not owed (NoRefusalBesideParked), and no live claim is released and no unserved client closed for a fresh one. The placed cap excludes raw pending arrivals: the inbox and current placement batch can each hold another cap, so accepted sockets can reach three times the cap plus the listener's current accepted socket; this is not a physical descriptor cap. The parked connections together hold at most PARKED_BYTES_PER_LANE (MAX_CONTROL_REPLY_LINE_BYTES) per request lane of unread answers and unfinished requests: past it the stalest holding any is closed (a live claim holder last, and before it one whose peer took bytes of its answer within TAKING_SPAN, so a steady reader is never closed for an answer parked unread beside it), never the last; an idle parked connection holds no buffer; an unsent answer of SPILL_FROM or more leaves the heap for an anonymous mapping unmapped once it is delivered or its connection closes (an answer carrying a secret segment stays in its guarded storage), and a request of SPILL_FROM or more still arriving is gathered into one sized for the whole of it and served from it, unmapped once consumed; a close for the budget or for a fresh client that panics costs that connection alone. A wait moves to a free wait lane, carrying the requests pipelined behind it. With every wait lane taken, a wait runs inline on its request lane only within limits.inline; past that it is answered CONTROL_BUSY_REPLY at once, with its connection kept and parked. A new client gets the busy reply only when every request lane holds a working request, and a freed lane admits again. Requests on one connection are answered in order, whichever lanes serve them. A connection's serial is stable across lanes, and its claims are released exactly once when it ends, however it ends. A panic while one parked connection wakes costs only that connection and does not count toward the parker's stop. A panic in the parker loop restarts it over the same parked set. A parker that cannot go on closes every connection it holds (claims released), and the lanes serve on without parking. Closing a connection shuts it in both directions, so a half-closed client reads EOF even though another descriptor survives. As the negative controls, the no-parker configuration (the pre-2026-09-26 design) violates NoIdleHold, and a cap that refuses beside parked connections (the pre-2026-10-19 design) violates NoRefusalBesideParked.	control_lanes_conformance.rs::shipping_lanes_conform_to_the_lane_tenure_model, control_lanes_conformance.rs::a_process_holding_the_cap_does_not_starve_a_fresh_client,
