```tsv
crates/aterm-gui/src/seamless_fixture_tests.rs::a_consumer_that_loses_or_moves_a_settings_draft_fails_the_drafts_check	keep	After the real shipped-wire reader adopts unchanged parent bytes, silently losing a draft, counting it unreadable, or moving it to another leaf must fail the consumer-placement check while the parent digests and proof remain valid. A flat draft-list check and wire-tamper controls miss these cases.
crates/aterm-gui/src/seamless_fixture_generator_tests.rs::generate_handoff_fixtures	keep	Runs its real producer and consumer in an isolated child, generating and validating every desk in private scratch storage by default, then holds every desk it wrote to the desk guard's own per-desk check (seamless_fixture_tests.rs::assert_written_desks_adopt) and reads them through the shipped-state sweep (serde_corpus_tests::shipped_state_with). An explicit release output keeps required release pins, and ATERM_SHIPPED_STATE_OUT keeps the sweep's answers file for the release's landing.
crates/aterm-gui/src/seamless_fixture_generator_tests.rs::generate_rendezvous_fixture	keep	Captures real rendezvous traffic in an isolated child and writes a private fixture by default; the release cutter supplies its destination and pins.
crates/aterm-gui/src/session_program.rs::park_for_a_read	move-to-bench	The body of a stand-in process for a_live_child_is_measured_against_its_real_parent. It does nothing unless a release file names it, and samples nothing.
crates/aterm-gui/src/window_show_conformance.rs::the_defective_design_rejects_the_real_steps	move-to-bench	Negative control for the conformance replay. It shows the Buggy=1 model rejects the real steps, which checks that the model is not vacuous, not a property of the code. A proof of WS-MODEL-REFINE does not subsume it, and AGENTS.md requires a negative control beside a model binding.
crates/aterm-gui/tests/headless_event_loop.rs::headless_event_loop	move-to-bench	harness=false main-thread run of the winit headless backend (a dependency, not aterm-gui code). It is effectful (AppKit FFI, CoreFoundation run loop, threads, dispatch_sync) and includes timing judgements (slept >= DEADLINE, turns_while_waiting <= 2). The liveness property behind it (every proxy clone wakes the loop, NSApp stays nil) belongs to winit's headless backend under gaps 8 and 13. Most of the file is its own libtest CLI emulation.
```

## 3. Suspicious tests

- crates/aterm-gui/src/app_config.rs::restart_notices_flags_columns_and_lines_but_nothing_else: the name and doc say only columns/lines raise a notice, but restart_notices also emits a gpu notice when old.gpu != new.gpu; the test never exercises gpu, so its implied spec ('nothing else') is false. The spec restart-notices states both lines.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/app_colorscheme.rs::appearance_flip_nudges_every_window: it only checks appearance_redraw_targets() = keys(windows), a one-line definitional body; the claim in its doc (sync_app_theme_to_appearance nudges every window when the theme is unchanged) is not observed. Folded into appearance-sync, which states the real obligation.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/app_config.rs::matrix_rain_cfg_tests: the module is named for matrix rain but 11 of its 22 tests are [packages], [update], [machine] and [privacy] resolver tests (mislabelled grouping); mapped to cross-reader-agreement, update-settings and privacy-resolution.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/app_config.rs::live_theme_file_swap_retains_valid_catalog_until_recovery: 'active.resolve("Work") is still Ok after a rejected scan' is guaranteed by value semantics (active is never mutated); only the Err(FileUnavailable) half samples a spec.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/app_config.rs::path_feed_fingerprints_enforce_the_loader_specific_caps: asserts the literal constants MAX_PATH_FEED_OPEN_ATTEMPTS = 17 and MAX_PATH_FEED_FINGERPRINT_READ_BYTES = 2_883_601 (constant pinning) besides the cap-equivalence property.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/app_config.rs::zero_seed_derives_stable_per_window: asserts seeds differ between WindowId(0) and WindowId(1); distinctness is a property of the particular hash, not something the code guarantees for all window pairs. rain-window-seed only claims nonzero and deterministic.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/app_config.rs::w6_font_config_warns_and_skips_unresolvable: correctness depends on the host font database not containing 'definitely-not-a-real-font-xyzzy' and on a fixture font path in another crate; environment-dependent.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/app_config.rs::the_shipped_windows_face_reaches_the_standard_band: Windows-only and host-font dependent, but its assertion follows from synthetic-band-head for any cell height, so the font measurement adds nothing.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/a11y_tree.rs::message_ids_round_trip_are_stable_and_are_never_read_as_a_tab: pins ChromeMessage::ORDER.len() == 7 (constant pinning) alongside the real round-trip property.
- chunk accounting: crates/aterm-gui/examples/objc_devtools_helper_drive.rs, objc_live_class_audit.rs and objc_toolbar_drive.rs contain no #[test] fns; the chunk's count of 277 includes 4 '#[test]' mentions in their doc comments. Real #[test] fns in this chunk: 273.
- app_input.rs::erase_price_memory_tests::large_commits_keep_only_the_bounded_erase_tail_without_retaining_their_allocation: asserts capacity() < 4*CAP and reference.capacity() > 2*CAP. Vec growth and drain-retention policy are not std guarantees, so the spec should bound only what trim and chunked extend control.
- app_input.rs::ledger_key_tests::cmd_shift_l_composes_the_focused_sessions_ledger_command: also pins the roster label prose 'Harness Log for This Tab'.
- app_input.rs::tone_status_tests::a_live_build_reports_the_classified_mood_and_that_the_model_ran: pins 'volume=0.40', a default value, inside a substring check.
- app_input/egress_contract_tests.rs::the_conpty_route_sends_every_key_through_the_ordered_writer: 'never written' is checked by a 50 ms sleep then read ≤ 0, a timing-dependent absence check.
- app_input/egress_contract_tests.rs::repeated_maximum_pastes_plateau_and_teardown_unblocks_every_waiter: the negative control 'still parked' rests on a 300 ms sleep.
- app_input/egress_contract_tests.rs::closing_the_session_releases_its_parked_writer_and_queued_input: the negative control rests on a 300 ms sleep.
- app_input_favourite_kitty_tests.rs::a_declining_window_or_search_action_refuses_in_words: toggle_fullscreen has no positive control (the comment admits it), so an always-refusing arm passes.
- app_input_keystroke_press_side_effect_tests.rs::typing_press_snaps_and_deselects_inert_and_repeat_and_release_do_not: its inert-modifier half duplicates app_input_press_path_lock_elision_tests.rs::a_bare_modifier_or_lock_key_is_inert.
- app_input_smooth_scroll_tests.rs::a_gesture_end_starts_the_rest_settle_at_once: bounds end_after against a fresh Instant::now(). This holds as an upper bound, but the handler reads the real clock.
- app_input_find_field_key_tests.rs::every_seeded_paste_spelling_pastes_into_the_query: its Windows branch (plain ctrl+v seeded) never runs on macOS/Linux CI, so that row of the spec is unsampled here.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/app_input_typed_kitty_summon_tests.rs::ime_and_external_local_boundaries_retire_older_candidates_before_consumers -- the second half pins source text: include_str! of app_input.rs, lib.rs, control_media.rs and toolbar.rs, including `matches("clear_tab_surface_move_license").count() == 7`. That is prose-pinning: any refactor breaks it and it proves nothing about compiled code. Delete that half; the behavioural half is spec move-licence-fences.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/app_native_packages_argv_tests.rs::apply_now_is_refused_under_a_private_state_root_and_nothing_else_is -- the second half scrapes app_native.rs for text order (refusal before the busy gate before the spawn; pass_lead adjacent to the verb). That is prose-pinning.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/app_input_typed_kitty_summon_tests.rs::a_backspace_erasing_a_zero_width_glyph_gives_back_a_priced_nothing -- its oracle committed_grapheme_cells_into is #[cfg(test)]-only, a test twin of ErasePriceMemory::price_graphemes. State the spec on price_graphemes and committed_text_cells, and delete the twin with the test.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/app_introspect.rs::strip_version_line_reports_what_was_laid_out -- assumes the test binary is a dev build (comment: it 'always has a short rung'). Under release build metadata strip_version_label(Short) is None, so the fixture would fail rather than the code.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/app_introspect.rs::empty_ledger_note_separates_measured_zero_from_unmeasurable -- pins prose substrings (`MEASUREMENT GAP`, `3 of them`, `are not input attempts`). The real spec is that the cases are disjoint and the note is JSON-safe; the wording assertions are prose-pinning.
- src/app_native_tests.rs::real_passing_refusal_keeps_a_deadline_as_the_model_s_passing_failure: the doc promises a Tier-1 conformance with a negative control (PassingFailureConverges), but the body ends after `let model = …;`, apparently lost in a merge. It is a green test that checks nothing, and project_passing_failure is unused.
- src/app_render_active_pane_mark_tests.rs::the_repaint_key_term_is_zero_for_no_mark_and_moves_with_the_rectangle: asserts key_term(left) ≠ key_term(right), which is DefaultHasher non-collision, not a universal property. Only `0 for None, odd for Some` is provable. Pack the rect injectively, or drop the distinctness clause.
- src/app_rename.rs::a_keystroke_in_the_field_moves_the_strip_fingerprint and src/app_native_tests.rs::native_appearance_inputs_have_distinct_cache_revisions: if these fingerprints are hashes, `≠` samples non-collision. The provable spec is that the input is included, as stated.
- src/app_palette.rs::the_menu_bar_publishes_what_the_palette_resolves: its doc claims the bar publishes what the palette resolves, but publish_menu_live sets has_selection=true whenever a native view is front, while palette_live uses native_selection_text().is_some(). The two disagree on a native front, and the test only checks a terminal front.
- (deleted 2026-10-16 with the presence row, timing-dependent:) src/app_presence.rs::review_r2_a_lapsed_drive_lease_lifts_the_rim and src/app_presence.rs::a_carried_lease_is_lapsed_on_time_after_the_commit: both used std::thread::sleep(60ms) against the real µs clock, which is timing-dependent (AGENTS.md). The spec should be driven through the injected presence clock.
- (deleted 2026-10-16 with the presence row:) src/app_presence.rs::the_tabs_retry_countdown_ticks_on_the_presence_timer_while_a_plan_stands: mixed the wall clock (aterm_time::unix_secs) with the test presence clock and asserts a 178..=180 window, so it is load-sensitive.
- src/app_native_tests.rs::durable_marker_is_observed_before_installed_bundle_identity: its 'negative control' catch_unwinds a local closure that asserts on its own Cell, which is tautological and exercises no shipping code.
- src/app_render.rs::a_cjk_title_is_a_band_title_on_its_first_frame_and_asks_one_frame_more, src/tab_bar.rs::a_cjk_title_is_a_band_tab_on_its_first_frame_with_its_hairlines, src/tray_raster.rs::a_cjk_label_has_its_chain_face_parsed_when_the_band_asks and src/tray_raster.rs::the_startup_warm_parses_the_cjk_and_hangul_faces_only: each returns early, passing, when no CJK chain face (or no band UI face) exists on the host, so it is vacuous on such machines. So are the Windows-only src/tray_raster.rs::a_quiet_labels_east_asian_text_inks_like_its_latin_and_the_selected_ones_is_semibold, a_semibold_run_never_borrows_the_regular_east_asian_face, a_cjk_label_has_its_weights_own_ui_faces_parsed_when_the_band_asks, the_startup_warm_parses_the_ui_faces_east_asian_faces_at_both_weights and src/tab_bar.rs::each_labels_east_asian_faces_are_its_own_weights on a Windows without Yu Gothic UI and Malgun Gothic.
- (deleted 2026-10-16 with the presence row, whose cached row it read:) src/app_presence.rs::review_r9_a_cache_hit_on_the_frame_path_does_not_allocate: part of it pinned pointer identity, an allocation or perf property.
- src/app_render_canonical_layout_scheduler_tests.rs::every_frame_route_threads_one_visible_plan / terminal_capture_threads_one_fresh_visible_plan: pin a #[cfg(test)] build counter (== 1, and == 3 for the control), a cost property tied to the current call graph rather than to observable behaviour.
- src/app_render_cursor_fx_generation_fence_tests.rs (3 curtain tests) and src/app_render_cursor_scroll_signal_tests.rs::an_erase_does_not_reset_the_cursor_effects_and_the_ribbon_survives_it / seventeen_band_moves_between_presents_fall_back_to_invalidate: the seams (retire_torn_cursor_fx, the scroll invalidation) read Instant::now() inside production code, and the tests offset t0 by -300 ms or -500 ms to compensate. That is a hidden wall-clock dependency (timing-sensitive under load). The curtain spec needs an injected clock before it can be proved.
- src/app_render_message_band_visual_tests.rs::the_web_band_golden_is_this_hosts_band: a golden snapshot rewritten with ATERM_BAND_GOLDEN=write. It pins host pixels to a file rather than stating parity with the web band, and regenerating it after any band change makes it vacuous. The spec should be a direct host-to-web equivalence.
- src/app_render_drop_overlay_tests.rs: apply_drop_overlay, apply_drop_overlay_at, composite_tray and composite_tray_at are #[cfg(test)] shims. The tests reach the production apply_overlay_at and composite_tray_quad_at only through test-only wrappers with fixed constants, so specs must target the production functions directly.
- src/app_render_tiled_seam_oracle_tests.rs::a_host_write_into_the_composite_revokes_the_retention_only_when_it_says_so: the undeclared arm asserts that poison cells SURVIVE (kept > 0 && survivors > 0). It pins the lane's unsoundness against undeclared writes as the contract. That is acceptable only if every host mutator is proved to bump snapshot_seq (an obligation no test checks).
- src/app_render_rain_host_tests.rs::shell_execute_edge_model_proves_and_catches_level_refresh: its ty_model! model is defined inside a test file, so the spec lives in #[cfg(test)] code. AGENTS.md puts models in crates/aterm-spec/src/derive.rs with a conformance test.
- src/app_render_message_band_raster_tests.rs::every_admitted_glyph_paints_a_non_blank_cell_headless and src/app_render_terminal_cursor_color_tests.rs::osc21_dynamic_cursor_tracks_osc10_in_main_frame_pixels_and_wake: both silently skip their renderer half when no system monospace font exists, so they pass vacuously on such hosts.
- src/app_render_message_band_raster_tests.rs::a_capture_at_an_injected_instant_is_deterministic uses std::thread::sleep(40 ms) to show wall-clock independence: a timing dependency in a test.
- src/app_render_single_hold_redraw_tests.rs::single_pane_glow_handoff_reuses_buffers_and_erases_on_disable mixes allocation-identity assertions (as_ptr equality, a bench property) with the erase-on-disable semantics. Only the latter is subsumed by cursor-trail-master-gate, and the pointer half should move to a bench.
- src/app_render_motion_policy_tests.rs::trail_status_reads_the_focus_the_frame_path_used, trail_status_intensity_folds_the_enable_gate and src/app_render_terminal_cursor_color_tests.rs::trail_status_names_the_style_that_owns_the_block_fill parse substrings of a printed status line (' block_fill=rainbow', ' intensity=0.00'). They pin prose formatting. The spec should be stated over a structured status record.
- src/app_render_tab_strip_bleed_tests.rs::the_build_badge_sits_below_the_strip (cfg windows) never runs on the macOS dev machine, so its spec is unexercised there.
- src/app_render_motion_policy_tests.rs::shed_latch_flap_backoff_bounds_transitions asserts 'transitions <= 14' and 'shed_frames > 3/4': magic-number bounds of a simulated oscillator. The real spec is a closed-form bound in terms of PERF_SHED_DWELL_MIN and the backoff law.
- src/app_render_find_bar_splice_tests.rs::find_bar_100k_history_work_is_logarithmic_plus_visible asserts work <= rows + 40 with '40' justified as two 17-step searches. The bound should be stated as 2*ceil(log2(n+1)) + rows so it scales with n.
- Fingerprint tests (src/app_restore_tests.rs::tab_label_rungs_fall_back_in_order_and_move_the_strip_fingerprint, src/app_search.rs::fingerprint_tracks_the_caret) use assert_ne! on FNV-1a hashes. That samples collision-freedom, which is false in general. Only determinism over the rendered fields is a valid spec.
- src/app_update_handoff_cold_lane_layout_tests.rs::a_layout_not_kept_is_said_on_record_once_the_switch_is_granted and ::a_refused_take_back_is_owed_until_it_lands_or_a_newer_write_replaces_it: each mixes a behavioural spec with a 'THE WIRING' half that greps app_update_handoff.rs for call order. Split them, and delete the source-pinning halves or restate them as effect-order specs.
- (deleted with the connected-spawn presets, owner surfaces S12:) src/app_tabs.rs::tab_menu_spawn_presets_connect_the_clicked_tab_not_the_front_one: checked the behaviour half only (tab_menu_subject).
- src/app_update_handoff_dialer_admission_tests.rs::a_candidate_signed_otherwise_is_caught_before_the_launch: it also asserts source order (read < fork < bind) through text search, in addition to the behaviour.
- Several tests poll with sleep loops bounded by a 60 s deadline (e.g. src/app_restore_tests.rs::the_handoff_layout_carries_the_agent_a_restored_tab_is_still_owed, src/app_settings.rs::a_devtools_hand_over_under_way_is_folded_into_the_park_and_read_by_its_tick). They fit AGENTS.md's hang-detector rule, but they are retry loops over worker threads, not deterministic steps.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/app_update_handoff_fork_lane_policy_wait_tests.rs::the_fork_lane_waits_while_the_policy_read_runs_and_parks_under_its_answer: its last third pins source text with include_str!/find (the fork lane's call order in app_update_handoff.rs). That is source pinning mixed into a behavioural test.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/app_update_handoff_fork_lane_policy_wait_tests.rs::a_read_in_flight_is_not_started_twice: its 'Wired' half greps app_native.rs for literal statements (RaiseOnDrop, passing.set, the absence of 'slot'). That is source pinning.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/app_update_handoff_fork_lane_policy_wait_tests.rs::a_read_that_ended_is_absent_or_outran_its_ceiling_is_not_waited_for and ::the_ceiling_outlasts_every_instant_a_read_can_hold_the_lock: both `return` early when Instant::checked_sub fails (for example on a fresh boot), so they can pass vacuously.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/app_update_handoff_late_park_record_tests.rs::a_hold_issued_during_the_commit_waits_for_the_attempt and ::a_topic_change_issued_during_the_commit_waits_for_the_attempt: the 'blocked while fenced' claim is only the absence of a reply within recv_timeout(300 ms). That is a latency budget, which the AGENTS rules forbid, and it cannot fail a fence that releases at 301 ms.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/app_update_handoff_handoff_process_group_tests.rs::a_launchservices_pid_mismatch_after_transfer_is_rejected_and_reaped: asserts started.elapsed() < 60 s ('immediate'), which is a latency budget, not a property.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/chrome_band.rs::install_forced_chrome_reports_only_real_movement and ::a_consumed_palette_edge_still_reaches_the_resample: under cfg(test), install_forced_chrome and forced_chrome use a thread-local slot, so these tests exercise the test-only branch. Only published_forced_chrome_is_all_or_nothing covers the shipping path (publish_forced_chrome, Windows only).
- crates/aterm-gui/src/band_raster_tests.rs::the_outlined_primary_keeps_the_accent_family_on_every_scheme: pins the borrower list to exactly ["Linen", "Catppuccin Latte"]. That golden table breaks on any theme addition and is not a property.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/band_raster_tests.rs::a_near_grey_cursor_borrows_blue_or_cyan_and_the_rest_keep_theirs: pins every builtin scheme's hue in a hand-written table ('every builtin scheme is pinned'). That is golden data, not the borrowing rule.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/claude_footer.rs::the_rule_carries_the_owners_footer: pins exact RGB values ([30,94,158] and [107,107,107]) and an exact reading string. These are golden colours beside the real layout property.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/app_update_screen.rs::apply_begins_charges_the_rim_and_a_refusal_restores_the_row: pins the literal row text 'Installing update — installing…', a prose pin inside a lifecycle test.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/band_motion_tests.rs::repeated_event_and_park_queries_share_the_next_visible_transition: asserts deadline_computations() counters (a memoisation cost). That is an implementation pin beside the value-equality property.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/claude_footer.rs::changed_claude_frame_reuses_free_row_buffers_but_preserves_held_snapshots and ::a_footer_written_again_allocates_nothing: allocation counts and raw-pointer equality are performance pins. Only their value and inverse parts are specs.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/app_update_handoff_returned_handoff_completion_lane_tests.rs::a_person_s_returned_handoff_never_spends_the_automatic_lane_s_budget (and the other schedule tests in that file): they assert retry deadlines inside 60 s windows measured from Instant::now() after the reduction. The schedule is a pure function that should be stated directly, and a stalled runner can fail these tests.
- src/control_auth.rs::ensure_private_dir_refuses_group_or_other_writable was mislabelled: its name and doc said a group/other-writable directory is REFUSED, but it only checked that ensure_private_dir accepts our own directory and forces it back to 0700. Replaced by src/control_auth.rs::ensure_private_dir_hardens_ours_and_refuses_a_strangers, which also refuses a stranger's 0700 and 0755 directories (control_auth_unix::ensure_private_dir_as).
- src/control_auth.rs::launch_sweep_removes_only_aged_empty_socks_nobody_listens_on retries the sweep up to 40 times, 25 ms apart (a 1 s budget). That breaks the AGENTS rule that a check never retries and that waits are one-minute hang detectors.
- src/control_auth.rs::random_token_is_64_hex_chars asserts that two draws differ. Distinctness is probabilistic, so it is not a provable spec. Only the 64-hex shape is a spec.
- src/claude_lights.rs gesture_tests: the shared pty() helper judges that bytes are ABSENT by waiting 30 ms (a timing-dependent negative check that many 'types nothing' assertions rely on). hang_up() waits up to 120 s, which breaks the one-minute hang-detector rule.
- src/clipboard_x11.rs::cross_client_clipboard_round_trip sleeps 100 ms so ownership can register (timing-dependent). It also returns a pass when there is no X display, so it can pass vacuously.
- src/clipboard_win.rs::set_then_get_round_trips_including_multibyte returned early as a pass when the clipboard was held, its later asserts sat under 'if set(..)', and it wrote the developer's own clipboard. Replaced 2026-10-18 by the_real_clipboard_round_trips_on_a_private_window_station, which asserts every step on a window station of its own.
- src/cli.rs::render_flags_ride_the_launch_struct_and_the_last_renderer_flag_wins mixes a behavioural check with a source-text scan (no 'aterm_log::env::set(' in cli.rs). The scan half pins prose, not behaviour.
- src/cli.rs::the_headless_flag_is_recorded_and_exports_nothing says 'exports nothing' but never checks the environment. It asserts only the Cli field and the help text.
- src/control.rs::a_per_process_candidate_publishes_only_after_the_commit: the behavioural half is sound, but the source-pin half matches whitespace-exact text of spawn's body and a 200-character window of lib.rs. That is brittle prose pinning.
- src/control_host.rs::a_cmd_block_cwd_is_where_its_command_ran tests aterm-core's OSC 133/633 block cwd attribution, not GuiHost. It belongs in aterm-core.
- src/consent_retire.rs::a_second_press_while_live_starts_nothing relies on a 200 ms sleep in the fake census to keep the first worker live when the second start runs (timing-dependent).
- src/config_watcher.rs stamp tests (config_metadata_edge_tracks_..., config_stamp_tracks_..., theme_stamp_tracks_..., a_lexicon_edit_...) assert_ne on 64-bit DefaultHasher outputs. Collisions are possible, so the sound spec is on the hashed metadata tuple, with ctime/inode movement as a platform assumption.
- crates/aterm-gui-consent/src/consent_card.rs's entry-words test (now the_entry_line_names_the_cause_and_the_tab_it_knows, its copy pins deleted) pinned prose fragments (banned-word lists, substrings); src/connections.rs::first_use_notice_names_the_authority_direction_and_the_undo did too, and went with the connection card (owner surfaces S12). They are kept as table properties only because they encode owner copy rules. Under the delete-prose-pinning rule they are candidates for removal.
- src/consent_observer.rs::the_sentinel_stream_is_bounded_by_a_timeout_and_rotated_on_eof asserts constants equal to literals (SENTINEL_TIMEOUT == "15m"), which is tautological. Only the lookup_args injection fence and the argument shapes are real properties.
- src/control_hangup_tests.rs::a_half_closed_caller_still_gets_its_answer also asserts elapsed >= 600 ms, a wall-clock lower bound on a timeout path.
- src/command_registry.rs::menu_faces_carry_stable_identities pins nine rows of a roughly 70-row table. The real spec (CMD-menu) is the whole table plus id injectivity, which no test checks.
- Chunk metadata: wave2-chunks.json lists 340 tests for part 9, but there are 338 #[test] fns. crates/aterm-gui/src/control_redraw_conformance.rs has ZERO #[test] fns: the two hits are the text `#[test]` in its module doc ('Why a binary and not a `#[test]`'). It is a harness=false binary gate (run_redraw_conformance), not a unit test.
- control_media.rs::an_invoked_close_tab_journals_its_caller_not_a_human ends with a source-text pin on lib.rs (that the InvokeMenuAction arm runs inside invoke_attributed). The behavioural half belongs to wire-tab-close-guard; the source half is prose-pinning.
- control_media.rs::capture_timeout_reports_err_only_when_cancellation_wins and ::video_timeout_awaits_commit_winner_instead_of_returning_err judge 'no answer yet' with recv_timeout(50 ms). That window passes vacuously when the waiter is slow, the same pattern control_socket_handoff_tests' own docs reject. The 60 s recv after it is fine.
- control_session.rs::a_count_at_the_manifest_limit_never_wedges_the_commit recomputes the ceiling inline (minted.saturating_add(TURN_ID_RESERVE).min(max)) instead of calling turn_ids_for_handoff. It checks past_ceiling against a re-implementation of the clamp, not the shipped one.
- control_session.rs::a_turn_across_an_update_park_presses_submit_once uses a real 1200 ms timeout for the parked arm, and idle_waits_do_not_latch_on_a_parked_readers_silence uses timeout=400 windows. The parked expectations are timing-coupled; the doc admits this only for the unparked arm.
- control_query.rs::modes_frames_its_count_over_distinct_key_lines exists because prose drifted from code. It is a const-evaluable table property and belongs in a const assertion or one generated table, not a per-verb test.
- consent_state.rs census/debugger/devtools tests use process-global static counters (RUNS, HARDENING_READS) reset per test. They stay serialized only because each test owns its own static; a second user of one counter would race.
- src/control_tests.rs::the_typed_turn_s_only_signature_is_its_even_cadence: asserts `total < nominal + 150` ms, a latency budget AGENTS.md forbids (a wait is a hang detector, never a budget); the key-tuple half is the spec, the upper timing bound should go.
- src/control_tests.rs::cross_session_paste_reports_a_dead_spill_peer_as_write_failed: retries up to 3 runs, skipping 'void' ones, contrary to 'a check never retries'; its verdict depends on a cloexec race the helper cannot close on Darwin.
- src/control_tests.rs::sequential_acknowledged_replies_never_exhaust_the_handoff_pool and detached_peer_without_a_valid_ack_is_still_quarantined: return early unless test_alone::alone(), so in a normal shared-process run they pass without asserting anything.
- src/control_tests.rs::quarantined_reply_holds_production_handoff_capacity: returns early unless enter_low_nofile_test_child(96), so the parent process passes vacuously.
- src/crash_signal.rs::a_killed_owner_releases_its_lock: prints SKIP and passes when /usr/bin/perl is absent.
- src/control_tests.rs::an_explicit_selector_for_the_front_tab_is_routed_through_the_input_seam: bundles three unrelated functions (front_routed, InputRoute::of, front_surface_authority) under a name that describes only the first.
- src/control_tests.rs::a_hard_lease_holds_every_other_connection_and_its_own_types_through: sets the thread-local SERVING_CONNECTION and resets it only at the end, so a failing assertion leaks state into later tests on the same thread.
- Chunk count mismatch: wave2-chunks.json says 343 tests for aterm-gui part 11, but the 22 listed files hold 368 #[test] fns. Both grep and brace-aware extraction agree on 368; fabric_launch alone has 13.
- crates/aterm-gui-fabric/src/lib.rs::post_wait_ack_returns_the_verdict_or_the_expiry_and_is_bounded_by_dl asserts waited < 10 s as an upper latency budget, and sleeps 600 ms to stage the scenario. AGENTS allows only a one-minute hang detector, never a latency budget.
- diagnostics.rs::host_validation_reports_only_authored_launch_flag_masking returns early unless crate::test_alone::alone(), so in an ordinary suite run it asserts nothing.
- diagnostics.rs::validate_flags_shadow_and_collision makes its two shadow assertions conditional on HARDCODED_SUPER_CHORDS. Where that is false (Linux) they check only an absence.
- fabric_launch.rs::filter_child_env delegates to aterm_types::env_sanitize::is_ai_env_key. The name says AI-tool keys, but the test requires it to strip aterm's own identity, edge, link and fabric secrets (ATERM_EDGE_*, ATERM_SESSION_ID, ATERM_LINK_*, ATERM_FABRIC_COMMAND). The function name mislabels the policy. a_non_utf8_key_with_a_denied_prefix_does_not_reach_the_bridge_child also duplicates aterm-types' own a_non_utf8_key_is_classified_by_its_lossy_spelling.
- defterm_win.rs, explorer_win.rs and file_picker_win.rs are #![cfg(windows)], so their 21 tests never run on the macOS or Linux dev hosts. defterm_win::current_delegation_reads_the_live_machine_without_erroring and file_picker_win::the_shell_picker_is_available_on_this_machine read the live machine (HKCU, COM).
- (deleted 2026-10-16 with the presence row and its DriverGeometry model:) driver_geometry_conformance.rs::a_pending_fold_never_lands_between_a_drivers_read_and_its_fenced_turn slept 5 ms to separate two Instants (read_at and the look). The sleep is load-bearing for the ordering, not a hang detector.
- crates/aterm-gui-fabric/src/lib.rs: two waits (a_parked_waiter_is_woken_by_a_down_report_from_starting_or_up, a_parked_post_learns_the_bridge_died_rather_than_timing_out) bound their spin by an iteration count (5_000_000 yields) rather than by aterm_spec::wait::MUST_HAPPEN, so the hang detector's length depends on machine speed.
- src/foreground_handback_conformance.rs::foreground_handback_a_mixed_batch_is_cut_at_the_park retries up to 5 attempts until the load-dependent one-batch shape appears. AGENTS.md says a check never retries. The spec it samples (handback-at-the-cut) is shape-independent, so the retry and the `one_batch` assertion should go.
- src/foreground_handback_conformance.rs::project_ownership sleeps a fixed 30 ms so a late modes-restored event can show before asserting NO new event. That is a timing-dependent negative assertion used by both ForegroundHandbackOwnership tests and by assert_not_the_replaced_rule.
- src/foreground_handback_conformance.rs::foreground_handback_liveness_is_probed_outside_the_term_lock opens by checking the #[cfg(test)]-only instrument crate::term_lock_held_on_this_thread. That part tests test code, not production.
- src/handoff_rendezvous.rs::a_grant_whose_connection_closes_at_once_is_still_claimed repeats to hit a race window ("Repeated because the window is a race"). It is timing-dependent sampling of a property the code should hold for every interleaving.
- src/handoff_carry_tests.rs::a_busy_lock_or_a_moved_archive_carries_the_counters_only asserts the constant LOCK_PATIENCE < 1 s, which is a latency budget, not a spec. The rest samples carry-lock-loss.
- src/descriptor_limit.rs::a_forked_successor_adopts_the_carried_launcher_limit pins source text with include_str!("app_update_handoff.rs") and include_str!("lib.rs") substring checks. That is prose/source pinning. Only its carried_launcher_limit rows sample a spec.
- src/handoff_carry_tests.rs::a_mangled_sidecar_never_panics_the_adopting_engine asserts `some > 20 && none > 20`, a property of its seeded mutation distribution, not of the code.
- src/handoff_history_tests.rs::stamps_round_trip_and_a_malformed_one_is_refused implies a canonical-form spec for parse_stamp. That spec is false: u64::from_str accepts a leading '+', so "+4096 <hex> +777" parses to the same fields as the canonical stamp. The same holds for parse_grant_body ("+7:+42"), WarmHint::parse and carried_launcher_limit. Decide whether '+' should be refused before stating the specs as canonical.
- src/handoff_history_tests.rs::the_shipped_producer_is_this_builds_export_but_the_strip compares the live export with a test-only re-implementation of the v0.94-v0.97 producer (shipped_export). The reference is test code, so the spec should state the frame format directly (history-export-frame-format).
- src/handoff_carry_tests.rs::a_desk_whose_ledgers_overflow_the_aggregate_keeps_every_sessions_newest_turns asserts total > 9/10 of MAX_AGGREGATE_BYTES. That is an efficiency bound that holds for this fixture, not a consequence of the core_shares spec in general.
- Chunk metadata: wave2-chunks.json says aterm-gui part 13 has 314 tests, but its 9 files hold 343 real #[test] fns. A naive grep finds 344 because hwkey.rs has a `#[test]` inside a doc comment ahead of parse_hwkey. Other chunks' counts may be off the same way.
- inject_floor::floor_throttles_a_tight_loop_then_recovers: the name promises recovery, but the body never checks it. Its bound (admitted <= 5) depends on the wall-clock refill between calls and on the process-global FLOOR state, so it is timing-dependent. Restate it on a pure step with injected time.
- host_exceptions_tests::every_host_entry_passes_the_door_and_the_caps: the doc says the reason is at most 90 characters, but the assertion allows 90 + 24 = 114. Either the cap or the doc is stale.
- host_exceptions_tests::a_repaint_that_gave_up_is_one_line_and_none_for_a_healed_epoch: the test branches on whether the headless App happens to have a pool session, and returns early on one branch. One run checks only the entry's wording, the other only that a non-at-risk epoch raises nothing. The doc's 'a registered one: the line, then its end' is checked on neither branch.
- harness_host_tests::a_worker_winding_down_is_stopped_once_not_at_every_pass: the cuts == 1 half samples a real spec. The passes < 10_000 bound over a 200 ms sleep is a loose ratio that other tests' bells also feed, as its own doc admits.
- harness_host_tests::the_real_host_conforms_to_the_leave_model: by its own doc, alive/ours/stray/named are what the driver did, due comes from the model, and the negative controls fire Buggy actions on model state alone. So it shows the model tells the buggy hosts apart, not that this host would be caught, and VisitNoLook is not caught here. It is weaker conformance than its name says.
- harness_host_tests::the_real_host_conforms_to_the_worker_lifecycle_model: its negative controls (Buggy=1, the badged projection) are likewise model-side only, except the Off let-go that the_lifecycle_projection_catches_a_real_let_go_of_an_off_session adds and the identity-only admission of a vendor Codex that the_real_host_admits_no_worker_for_a_vendor_codex runs on the real host.
- harness_netprobe::the_route_reads_every_settings_source_claude_code_reads: most of what it checks is aterm-agent's claude_settings chain, which its own doc says is tested there. Only gather's wiring is this crate's, so the spec should live in aterm-agent and this becomes a wiring check.
- hwkey::pacing_tokens_are_additive_and_bounded: the tokens are not additive. Count and interval are independent fields and only mods are OR-ed, so the name misdescribes the property.
- src/level_up.rs::fingerprint_is_nonzero_stable_per_frame_and_steps: the assert_ne!s across frames and across builds depend on hash non-collision. Only 'non-zero' and 'constant within a frame' are provable.
- src/lib.rs::empty_is_zero_and_text_and_caret_both_move_it: assert_ne!(a, 0) and 'text moves the key' are false in general, since fnv1a_64(p) ^ u64::MAX = 0 when fnv1a_64(p) = u64::MAX. Only 'the caret alone moves the key' holds for all inputs.
- src/lib_early_out_tests.rs::the_pane_selection_fold_changes_with_any_panes_selection: every 'changes the fold' assertion depends on DefaultHasher non-collision; the provable spec is weaker.
- src/lib.rs::a_confirmed_paste_reaches_its_owner_after_a_tab_switch_not_the_new_front: 'the front tab receives nothing' is judged by a 150 ms drain window, i.e. absence over a timed window.
- src/input_stall.rs::pid_cpu_ns_reads_a_spinning_child_in_nanoseconds: a ratio test (the reading must be within 2× of the reap's rusage), not an exact property.
- src/instance_retention_conformance.rs::real_instance_sweep_decision_conforms_for_entire_lease_pid_matrix: besides the conformance check, it polices the xref anchor and waiver registry ('only Decide is anchored'), which is a registry guard, not a spec of the code.
- src/lib_bottom_padding_geometry_tests.rs::gpu_crop_alignment_is_exact_for_every_parity_and_crop_direction: its last fixed assertion expects 0 on Linux and 4 elsewhere, so the implied spec depends on the platform's band_offset_y. The spec must be stated per target.
- src/lib.rs::rain_front_scheduler_model_proves_and_catches_native_wake_regression: it model-checks the ty_model! itself (prove_and_catch_scalar) and touches no shipping code. It belongs to the model-verification lane, not to a unit test.
- src/keymap.rs::lock_modifiers_reports_only_caps_lock_from_the_hid_system: assert_eq!(locks, lock_modifiers()) re-reads live HID state, so it races a person toggling Caps Lock during the run.
- src/input.rs::key_and_text_egress_complete_while_the_terminal_mutex_is_held: the implied spec is structural (the Key and Text arms never call term_lock), but the test samples it through threads and a 60 s receive timeout.
- src/kitty_log.rs::exit_detaches_a_filesystem_stalled_worker_at_the_deadline: it asserts behaviour at a wall-clock deadline (EXIT_JOIN_BUDGET), so it is partly a timing test.
- src/lib.rs::a_held_flip_wakes_on_two_quiet_looks_or_at_the_ceiling: the doc says 'the ceiling wakes it at once', yet the test asserts that a Ceiling look at 5·RECHECK returns false after earlier looks. The real rule lives in atpkg::quiet::Recheck::wake and should be recovered there before this is stated.
- lib_effect_cadence_tests.rs::the_effect_lane_presents_strictly_slower_than_the_panel_refreshes: the test implies effect_present_interval_with is total, but `effect_tick_interval(p) * periods.max(1)` uses Duration's panicking Mul. effect_present_interval_with(Some(Duration::MAX), 2) panics, and so do ws.effect_present_interval() and deco_anim_hold() (× DECO_ANIM_LEVEL_FRAMES) for a huge reported frame_interval. The spec needs a requires clause or the code needs saturating_mul.
- lib_global_cap_tests.rs::global_shed_order_picks_largest_until_under_cap: global_shed_order and enforce_scrollback_cap_at compute `usages.iter().map(..).sum()`, which panics on usize overflow in debug builds. The implied 'any usages' spec is false at the overflow boundary; the code should use saturating sums.
- lib_fifo_backlog_tests.rs::the_model_adds_one_per_present_and_drains_one_per_period: drained_to uses Duration::mul_f64, which panics on overflow or non-finite input (e.g. a huge period with a large level). The test samples only small values.
- lib_head_watch_park_tests.rs::a_private_windows_passes_lead_with_the_flag_and_the_owners_do_not: it mixes a behavioural spec (spawned argv) with a source scan counting a literal in lib.rs (include_str). The scan half is prose-pinning and should be dropped or moved to a wiring check.
- lib_session_teardown_identity_tests.rs::dropping_a_session_whose_pid_names_another_process_signals_nothing: its negative claim rests on a fixed 500 ms sleep past 'the old SIGKILL tick'. A timing window stands in for the spec 'Session::drop never signals an unverified pid', against AGENTS' rule that a wait is a hang detector, never a latency budget. dropping_an_adopted_session_before_commit_leaves_its_shell_alive and a_session_built_through_the_spawn_s_latch_keeps_only_an_uncommitted_adopted_shell use the same 500 ms survival window.
- lib_overlap_handoff_tests.rs::held_rekeys_are_written_by_the_commit_and_never_before: the uncommitted arm sleeps 300 ms and then asserts the key file is absent. That is a timing-bounded negative; the spec ('never written without a Commit') is not what the sleep checks.
- lib_multi_window_tests.rs::the_title_drift_gate_fires_for_a_newly_labeling_window_and_not_otherwise: the positive leg asserts only `flushed ∨ pending`, which is weaker than the gate's actual contract (immediate flush iff past the debounce interval, else pending).
- lib_effect_cadence_tests.rs::the_effect_train_runs_at_the_panels_refresh_within_its_floors: its 'negative control' asserts constant arithmetic about a deleted expression (capped − tick = 8 333 667 ns). It pins history rather than the function.
- lib_tests.rs::the_effect_lane_parks_within_two_seconds_of_the_last_key_under_v2: the 2 s bound is on the simulated clock (deterministic), but it is a tuning budget for the glow engine's idle time (≤ 1.54 s). If it is a spec it belongs to aterm-effects' engine, not to the host planner.
- src/markdown.rs::trims_and_is_idempotent_on_plain_text claims to_plain_text is idempotent, which is false in general. `# - a` becomes `- a`, which a second pass turns into `• a`. `# # x` becomes `# x`, which a second pass turns into `x`. `## 1) x` becomes `1) x`, which a second pass turns into `1. x`. It holds only on the sublanguage where no output line is again a heading, bullet, ordered item or hrule, so md-plain-text states it that way.
- src/menu.rs::the_version_menu_never_offers_the_running_build says 'an unnamed running build (0) filters nothing', but staged_for_version_menu keeps only build > running, so a staged build 0 is filtered. The spec is `build > running`, not 'nothing'.
- src/link_target.rs::a_tracked_pane_names_the_gesture_that_still_opens_the_link also asserts crate::app_mouse::press_starts_selection, which belongs to another module's spec.
- src/manual_reset.rs::reset_terminal_menu_row_resets_the_focused_session also pins MenuAction::ResetTerminal.writes_pty_input() = false and the palette row, which are menu classification facts mixed into a reset test.
- src/main_thread_probe.rs::the_probe_reads_a_spinning_threads_cpu_and_stack depends on the scheduler giving the spinner 50 ms of CPU within the hang bound. It is environment-dependent on a loaded machine (a hang detector, not a latency budget, but still a live-platform probe).
- src/message_reporters_tests.rs::every_reporter_message_survives_the_door quantifies only over a hand-kept test-only roster (`every_reporter_message`, `every_lane_message`). A new builder or input shape left off the roster is unchecked, so the stated 'every builder' claim is stronger than what runs.
- native_config_language.rs::machine_policy_domain_matches_atpkg_and_bad_types_remain_errors implies that atpkg reads universal_control = "OFF" (and "Leave" and "leav") as Leave. An upper-case opt-out silently fails open, while every registry enum is described as case-insensitive. Confirm this is intended in atpkg.
- native_config_host.rs::shipping_lane_conforms_to_latest_revision_model projects the pending slot by hard-coding (2,2) whenever the model's pending_revision > 0, instead of deriving it from model state. That is a weak conformance binding.
- native_appearance.rs::text_scale_is_sane_and_bounded samples only the NaN and upper clamp cases. The lower bound of normalized() is unspecified by the tests.
- The chunk manifest says 330 tests, but the 12 files hold 335 #[test] fns (metrics 54, native_accessibility 18, native_app 45, native_appearance 9, native_config_conformance 8, native_config_host 2, native_config_language 88, native_config_service 21, native_control_conformance 2, native_document_host 31, native_document_io 17, native_document_journal 40).
- crates/aterm-gui-documents/src/native_markdown.rs::parses_blocks_outline_links_images_and_stable_ranges asserts block.source().start < end (non-empty), while reader_hides_comments_but_preserves_code_and_canonical_ranges asserts only start <= end. The two tests imply inconsistent block-range specs; pick one (md-block-source-ranges uses strict).
- crates/amacs/src/editor/view.rs::forward_word_applies_a_count_in_one_pass_from_the_last_break: half of it is a cost bound read from the #[cfg(test)] thread-local EDITOR_WORDS_READ. That is a complexity property, not part of the functional word-motion spec, and belongs in a bench (or a separately stated cost spec).
- crates/amacs/src/editor/view.rs::backward_word_scans_a_long_token_once_and_applies_counts_in_one_pass: the name claims a single scan, but it asserts only result positions, with no scan count. The name is mislabelled relative to what it checks.
- crates/aterm-gui-documents/src/native_markdown.rs::inline_semantics_and_reading_source_map_retain_exact_authored_ranges: its second half checks the source_map of semantic_projection, which is #[cfg(test)] and has no production caller, so that half tests test-only code. Likewise reader_hides_comments, quote_continuations and tables_and_semantic_text use the #[cfg(test)] semantic_text as their oracle; their specs are restated on block texts.
- crates/aterm-gui-documents/src/native_markdown.rs::virtual_layout_materializes_a_bounded_window_with_source_anchors: part of its assertions run through the #[cfg(test)]-only move_block_anchor, which has no production caller.
- crates/amacs/src/editor/projection.rs: project_viewport and line_starts are #[cfg(test)] wrappers or oracles. The specs target the production project_viewport_with and line_starts_capped; the tests reach production only through those wrappers.
- native_font_catalog.rs::prepared_catalog_carries_exact_admitted_toy_pack_consumers pins specific capability booleans that depend on the content of the tiny-triumphs pack.toml data file. Only the equality assets.sparkle_spec_consumers == Some(sparkle.consumer_capabilities()) is a spec; the flag values pin the data.
- src/native_settings_tests.rs::choose_image_is_enabled_exactly_when_a_picker_exists - the doc comment says 'On this machine (Windows, with a real IFileOpenDialog)'; the assertion is platform-conditional (cfg macos|windows), so the prose is stale for the hosts that run it.
- src/native_settings_tests.rs::wide_search_page_one_lists_native_rows_beside_the_manual_result - asserts the literal '2 settings · 9 Manual config keys' and '2–3 of 3', counts that move with registry contents rather than with the property (native rows beside the Manual card on page 1).
- src/native_settings_tests.rs::the_log_at_its_ring_cap_builds_only_the_rows_in_view - the font_visits <= 2x small-log bound is a cost ratio, not a spec; the rows-built equality and out-of-view invariance are the spec. It also writes measurements to stderr.
- src/native_settings_tests.rs::native_about_byline_steps_down_to_the_longest_form_its_column_fits - at 2x the 240pt arm depends on the host UI face and prints a waiver to stderr instead of asserting the step-down, so the outcome differs by host font.
- src/native_settings_tests.rs::the_devtools_card_draws_what_it_measures - samples every_devtools_facts() with step_by(11) although the spec is over the whole finite space.
- src/native_settings_tests.rs::a_reset_invocation_can_never_hold_the_main_thread_open_ended - spawns real /bin/sleep (or ping) children inside a GUI unit test; the bounded-wait spec is an effect-lane property (gap 8), and a_prompt_invocation_is_reported_by_its_own_exit_code likewise spawns /usr/bin/true|false.
- src/native_settings_tests.rs::top_effect_controls_truthfully_escape_the_serious_mode_override - the expected edit lists are filtered by DEFAULT_DECORATIVE_EFFECTS; the platform-independent spec is the post-apply projection equality, the edit list is a platform-conditional consequence.
- crates/amacs/src/text.rs::large_text_is_chunked_balanced_and_round_trips - the module doc promises AVL height and logarithmic split/replace, but balance() is one rotation at the concat root and only from() is shown to be height-bounded; no test or spec covers the height after repeated replace, so the 'balanced' claim may not hold for edited ropes.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/native_update_auto_intent.rs::a_stage_a_person_installs_is_read_when_it_arms: half of it include_str!s app_native.rs and asserts byte distances (< 120) between source snippets and a count of call sites. That pins source text, not behaviour, and breaks on any reformat. Only the arm/arm_reads_candidate half is a spec (auto-intent-arm). The wiring claim needs a contract on arm_native_auto_apply or a call-graph check, not a text scan.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/owned_endpoint.rs::a_terminating_signal_removes_only_what_this_instance_still_owns: no signal is ever raised. The test calls Published::remove directly, so on_exit_signal, the sigaction install in publish, and the re-raise go untested despite the name.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/native_ui.rs::semibold_goes_only_where_a_slot_was_sized_with_room_to_grow_ink: its outline-row premise is searched for on the host's installed UI font, and the test panics when no qualifying heading exists. Its verdict therefore depends on the host font, not only on aterm code. The spec (ui-navigation-selection-marks) should be stated over measured widths, with no premise search.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/native_updater_service.rs::the_activation_identity_is_well_formed_pure_and_distinct: the distinctness asserts (one digest per build, never equal to a download digest) are SHA-256 collision facts. They can be assumed but never proved; only purity, format and case-insensitivity are provable.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/palette.rs::fingerprint_tracks_query_and_cursor and crates/aterm-gui/src/palette.rs::fingerprint_folds_the_realized_bucket: both assert that a hash changed (assert_ne on fingerprints), which a collision would falsify. The provable spec is only the dependency set plus a non-zero result.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/nudge_conformance.rs (all 6 tests): they run on the real wall clock (a 1 s risk wait and a 1.5 s person gate, about 4 s per schedule) against a real pty. They assert outcomes, but AGENTS.md treats timing-dependent tests as candidates for deletion. They should become a ty_model! nudge machine plus a conformance bind with an injected clock.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/pane_header.rs::header_cache_reuses_pixels_and_refreshes_title_focus_and_native_icon: reuse is asserted through pointer identity (Arc::as_ptr, Vec::as_ptr), which is an implementation detail. The observable spec is that the returned value is unchanged and nothing is repainted.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/presence.rs (most fixture tests): they classify through Cursor::Unknown, a #[cfg(test)]-only arm that calls reader.read instead of the shipping reader.read_at. They exercise a code path production never takes; the specs (agent-verdict-refines-phase-reader, agent-verdict-zone-cursor) must be stated and proved for Cursor::At, and a_relaunched_inline_repl_is_published_idle_only_at_the_box_that_holds_the_cursor's first assertion pins a known-wrong reading of that test-only path ('RED: the old box by its frame alone').
- crates/aterm-gui/src/presence.rs::classify_is_aterm_phases_verdict: its oracle is aterm_phase::read itself (the expected value is computed by the library under test).
- crates/aterm-gui/src/relaunch_notice.rs::fingerprint_tracks_build_and_is_nonzero: assert_ne!(a, b) for two builds is a DefaultHasher non-collision claim (with the low bit forced to 1), true at that sample but not a universal property; only fingerprint != 0 is a theorem.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/publish_when_committed_conformance.rs::a_candidates_entries_name_it_only_after_the_commit: the pre-Commit property is sampled by polling for a fixed 300 ms wall-clock window; the spec is 'for the whole interval the gate is closed', so the window is a timing-dependent sample, not the property.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/qos.rs::a_linux_slice_lands_on_the_declaring_thread_and_stops_there: returns early (passes) when the kernel ignores the slice request, so it is vacuous on pre-6.12 kernels.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/presence.rs::r44_hb5_the_reset_countdown_places_a_reset_with_the_offset_that_holds_then: returns early when the machine's zone keeps one offset and depends on `date` subprocess offsets; vacuous on UTC machines and measures the environment, not the function.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/proxy.rs::mirror_dir_only_for_out_of_default_instances and crates/aterm-gui/src/platform_win.rs::the_chrome_palette_is_forced_only_under_high_contrast: both return early (pass vacuously) under environment conditions (no per-user socket dir; diagnostic env override set).
- crates/aterm-gui/src/resize_ledger.rs: the five named-schedule tests (a_run_brought_back_to_zero_keeps_the_draw_it_saw, a_flap_split_by_a_frame_or_by_time_is_judged_on_the_real_engine, the_t2649_flap_is_undone_and_the_historical_engine_is_caught, the_assumed_repaint_answers_ok_on_a_tick_at_a_changed_size, a_quiet_flap_only_time_split_is_one_run_credited_back) replay schedules already inside resize_render_conformance's exhaustive walk (length <= 6); their only extra content is reply-string pins on the rig.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/platform.rs: user_input_age_is_recent and read_bounded_stdout are cfg(any(<platform>, test)); on the platforms where their tests usually run (macOS for the latter, Linux/Windows for the first) they are test-only code with no production caller, so a proof there is about dead code. portal_settings.rs is Linux-only, so its tests run only there (the Linux lane).
- crates/aterm-gui/src/prefs.rs::settings-registry tests (matrix_rain_row_surfaces_in_the_settings_model, packages_consent_rows_surface_in_the_settings_model): many assertions pin exact (group, order) pairs and labels per key, i.e. table contents restated in the test; only the cross-registry consistency is a general law.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/scroll_motion.rs::overscroll_resistance_laws: overscroll_resist(raw) computes raw.abs()*3, which overflows (panics in debug) for |raw| > i64::MAX/3 and on i64::MIN. The documented 'odd, monotone' laws need that precondition, and the lattice samples only |raw|<=1000.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/scroll_motion.rs::glide_converges_monotonically_and_exactly: glide_position computes target_px - start_px in i64, which can overflow, and goes through f64, which is exact only for |delta| <= 2^53. The documented 'never oversteps' invariant needs a precondition the doc does not state.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/scroll_motion.rs::overscroll_spring_bounces_and_self_disarms: add_impulse calls f64::clamp(-max_px, max_px), which panics when max_px < 0 or is NaN. No caller-side precondition is documented.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/session_program.rs::slow_lookup_coalesces_retries_and_serves_a_new_group_promptly: asserts that NO wake arrives within recv_timeout(50 ms). That is a timing-dependent negative, which AGENTS.md's rule forbids: a wait is a one-minute hang detector, never a latency budget.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/seamless_tests.rs::awaiting_the_parents_end_is_bounded_and_ends_with_the_parent: asserts wall-clock bounds (started.elapsed() >= bound and < MUST_HAPPEN). The spec belongs on await_parents_end's loop, with time treated as an effect.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/robi_bubble.rs layout/paint tests (also scroll_motion's glide and spring tests): every statement is over f32/f64. Trust has no float model, and the audit's section-7 gap table has no row for one, so these specs are blocked on a gap the audit does not list.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/seamless_fixture_tests.rs::every_release_since_the_floor_pins_the_required_desks: the cutter in aterm-release parses REQUIRED_DESKS out of this test file's source, so a production release gate depends on the text of a test.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/session_status_tests.rs::the_status_record_carries_the_effective_autopilot_beside_supervisor pins field ORDER through a substring of the formatted line. That is close to prose pinning; the spec is the record grammar.
- Chunk count: the chunk entry says 295 tests, but there are 294 #[test] fns. status_item.rs:1780 is the text "#[test]" inside a doc comment ("…`pthread_main_np()` is 0 inside a `#[test]`…"), which the chunker's grep counted.
- session_timeline.rs::the_upgrade_column_reads_the_awake_clock_as_it_stands_now: which branch it asserts depends on the host's real system_awake_since(). The assert_eq on past_grace makes it pass either way, so it pins only one side per machine. The awake clock should be injected so both sides are checked.
- snapshot_path.rs write_private* (3 tests): they drive #[cfg(test)]-only wrappers (write_private, absolute_lexical) that have no production caller. The property belongs to pinned_dir::PinnedDir::write_private, and the tests or spec should move there. The Windows test silently returns success when symlink privilege is missing.
- spawn.rs source-reading tests (8 spawn_session_* and the_seed_follows_…, plus the wiring half of an_adopted_timeline_opens_with_a_handoff_gap): they grep spawn.rs's own text through include_str! for exact call spellings, such as "handoff_commit: adopted_handoff_commit(adopted, recovered, factory.rekey_deferred.as_ref())," and a whitespace-stripped pulse call. They pin source formatting and names, not behavior: a semantics-preserving rename or rewrap fails them, while a wrong argument that keeps the spelling passes. They stand in for a call-order trace spec on spawn_session.
- settings_preview.rs pixel-difference thresholds (differences(..) > 20/40/80/120) in candidate_theme…, visual_settings_change…, exact_candidate_font_size…, the automatic_window_samples twins and resolved_custom_kitty_asset…: these measure how much changed, not a specification. Only the == 0 and fingerprint-equality halves are spec-shaped.
- settings_preview.rs audit/accessibility tests pin prose substrings ('portable SDR tone-map: bloom', 'fire shimmer', 'no panel-headroom claim', 'host-prepared renderer snapshot unavailable', 'resident cat companion'). That is prose-pinning. The spec-worthy predicates are the 240-byte bound, the absence of internal terms, the shipped-default token being named, and 'fails closed' iff the trail is unavailable.
- Hash-inequality assertions (status_item fingerprint tests; settings_preview fingerprint ≠ tests) assert assert_ne! on 64-bit hashes. They hold only up to collision. The provable claim is injectivity of the pre-hash tuple, which is stated in the specs.
- spawn.rs reply_writer_lifetime_tests (a_reattached_writer…, a_failed_spawn…) use std::thread::sleep(20/50 ms) then assert!(!join.is_finished()) as a negative. That is timing-dependent, which AGENTS.md forbids. deferred_reader_gate's 20 ms recv_timeout negative is similar, although guarded by a parked flag.
- session_waits.rs::a_large_paste_takes_its_row_and_stop_drops_only_its_rest polls until fill_permille >= 200 or a deadline, then asserts on whatever stats it has. If the deadline hits first, it asserts on a partial reading instead of failing as a hang.
- sound_seam.rs: HostWedged and SeamReason::ALL exist only under cfg(any(target_os = "macos", test)). Off macOS, the_seam_names_the_gate… checks a variant that a production build cannot construct.
- spawn.rs::identity_env_carries_the_parent_id… reads the ambient $TMUX and $STY of the test process, so its expected values are environment-derived rather than fixed.
- Scope drift: the chunk's 339-test count was taken on the main checkout. In the worktree, commit 64b1d6833 has already removed title_summary.rs (82 tests) and title_summary/model_store.rs (5 tests), plus 5 tab_bar label re-split tests (whole_label/shed_place/state_clause_bytes). Those 92 tests sample retired code, so no spec is owed for them. The main checkout's tab_label.rs has 10 tests while the worktree's has 11, so the worktree carries one test main lacks; that should be reconciled at merge.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/tab_menu.rs::fingerprint_is_zero_closed_nonzero_open_and_moves_with_the_highlight: assert_ne!(open, lit) depends on DefaultHasher not colliding. That is not a property a proof can claim. The spec states only the exact hash and that it is nonzero when open. If change detection must be guaranteed, compare a structural key instead of a hash.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/subscribe.rs cells tests (selection_*/style_policy_reload): the implied rule, re-emit whenever render-only state changes, rests on the u64 frame-key etag (render_sig inside it) and the body's (FNV-1a-64, length) id, either of which can collide. The provable spec is 're-read iff the etag differs, re-emit iff the body id differs' plus 'every listed field feeds the hash'.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/tab_bar.rs pixel_band tests (36): every one except the fit tests that use the closed-form wide_face/mono measures returns early with no assertion when the host has no UI face (with_ui_faces() == false). On a fontless CI host they pass vacuously. The fit_labels_distinctly specs need no fonts and should be proved first.
- toolchain_words.rs::byte_stats_keep_one_width_for_the_life_of_a_transfer: the claim 'one width from its first megabyte to its last' is false for the first megabyte. byte_stats(999_000, 74_000_000) = '999 KB / 74 MB' (14 chars) but byte_stats(74_000_000, 74_000_000) = '74 MB / 74 MB' (13). The pad width comes from fmt_bytes(total), which can be narrower than a 3-digit KB figure. The test only samples done >= 1_000_000, which hides this.
- trail_audio.rs::worker_lifecycle_conforms_and_parks_without_polling: uses fixed sleeps (10 ms, then 12 ms) as evidence that nothing opens before the first cue and that a paused worker does not tick. These negative checks depend on timing.
- trail_audio.rs::a_stalled_device_is_discovered_by_the_next_key_and_that_key_is_still_heard: sleeps 40 ms to pass the 16 ms healthy window, so the budget-restore half depends on scheduling.
- upgrade_host.rs::the_owners_words_are_written_one_at_a_time_in_the_order_pressed: the 200 ms sleep is what lets an overlapping (thread-per-press) implementation get caught. The pass does not depend on timing, but whether the negative is detected does.
- upgrade_exceptions_tests.rs (all 7): the classification table is aterm_agent's Row::attention; only upgrade_exceptions is aterm-gui code. The attention specs belong in aterm-agent.
- update_control.rs::the_restored_agents_hold_is_named_while_it_holds: mixes the posture ladder with checks in three other modules (native_update_auto_intent::restored_hold_line, harness_host::RESTORED_HOLD, aterm_types control-verb help text), including a prose pin ('seven minutes' in the help).
- tray_raster.rs::ui_faces_rasterize_and_bold_is_no_lighter: the doc says 'on supported desktops', but the test asserts bold > regular ink unconditionally. It depends on the host's UI faces and uses an ink-sum proxy.
- watchdog.rs::the_watchdog_is_armed_unless_explicitly_switched_off: the one behavioural assertion is skipped whenever the ATERM_WATCHDOG seam is set in the environment; the rest compares constants.
- toolchain_words.rs::pass_load_names_the_heaviest_active_phase: ends with assert_eq!(HEAVY_PASS_BYTES, 250_000_000), which pins a constant and has nothing to do with pass_load.
- toolbar.rs TabGeometry::separates (dividers test): 'index != active + 1' overflows (and panics in debug) at active = usize::MAX. Unreachable for real tab counts, but the spec needs the precondition.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/window_show.rs::stacking_ranks: when live contains duplicate ids, both copies get the same rank and the result is not a permutation. The docs assume distinct ids, and WS-RANK states that as a precondition.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/window_show.rs::commit_carried_window_show: re-keying is suppressed if ANY typed window differs from the key, even when the person's LAST keystrokes went to the key window. After key_typed_window has already re-keyed to the last-typed window, typed == [w2, key] still skips the Commit raise. The module docs agree ('typed into a different carried window'), but 'last typed' may be the intended rule.
- crates/aterm-gui/src/work_count_tests.rs::the_present_walk_touches_only_the_visible_panes_stamps: the first-walk bound PANES..=2*PANES is loose and not derived from the code; WORK-PRESENT-WALK takes the upper bound only.
- crates/aterm-gui/tests/headless_event_loop.rs::headless_event_loop: the grep-based chunk count of 1 comes from a doc-comment mention of '#[test]'. The binary has no #[test] attribute, so tooling that counts #[test] lines misreports this file.
